entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to quash the entire proceeding including the charge sheet dt. 10.8.2011 as well as 15. 10.2011 and cognizance order dated 5.11.2011 in case no. 308/2012 arising out of case crime no. 28/2011, u/s 498A, 323 I.P.C. and 3/4 of D.P. Act P.S. Mahila Thana Rakabganj, District Agra, State Vs. Rajesh and others, pending in the court of Civil Judge (Junior Division)/F.T.C. First, Agra on the basis of compromise.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that opposite party no.3 is the wife of applicant no.1 and other applicants no. 3,4, 5 and 6 are his family members and on account of matrimonial discord, present criminal case was instituted against the applicants, however, subsequently, with the intervention of respected members of both the families, the parties have settled all their disputes and differences and they have decided to live separately.

Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that a compromise deed dated 1.9.2022 has also been made between the parties, copy of which has been annexed as Annexure No. 4 to this application.
This Court vide order dated 6.12.2022 has directed the parties to appear before the court below and file compromise deed who shall verify the same and forward a report to this Court.
Pursuant to this order both parties have appeared before the court below and in presence of the parties the court below has verified the compromise deed vide order dated 29.9.2022.
The copy of which has been provided to this Court and has been filed today and taken on record.
Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that in view of the said compromise, entire criminal proceedings be quashed.
Learned A.G.A. has no objection, if the entire proceeding is quashed.

This Court is not unmindful of the judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of:-
(1). B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675. (2).
Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation [2008) 9 SCC 677].

sentences.text: Wherein, Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held that compromise can be made between the parties even in respect of certain cognizable and non-compoundable offences.

Reference may also be made to the decision given by this Court in Shaifullah and others Vs. State of U.P. and another [2013 (83) ACC 278], in which, law expounded by Hon'ble Apex Court in the aforesaid cases has been explained in detail.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose shall be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned case.

Accordingly, the entire proceedings of case no. 308 of 2012 arising out of case crime no. 28/2011,
u/s 498A, 323 I.P.C. and 3/4 of D.P. Act P.S. Mahila Thana Rakabganj, District Agra, State Vs.
Rajesh and others, pending in the court of Civil Judge (Junior Division)/F.T.C. First, Agra are hereby quashed.
